study_identification.title: Cortical thickness and grey-matter volume anomaly detection in individual MRI scans: Comparison of two methods

study_characteristics.study_objective: To compare the performance of an open-source research-level tool for detection of statistical anomalies in individual MRI scans, 'ScanOMetrics', depending on whether it is operated on the output of FreeSurfer or of the deep learning based brain morphometry tool DL + DiReCT.

quality_checking_detail.answer: The LOOCV analysis was used to identify anomalous scans separately for the DL + DiReCT and FreeSurfer pipelines and remove them from the normative datasets. Scans were considered not (entirely) normal if they yielded p-values lower than q = 0.01 for 18 or more out of the 358 raw metrics (5 % of metrics). 99 HC scans with large number of anomalies (5.15 %) were removed.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Covariates other than age (i.e. sex, scanner and scanning protocol) were accounted for by selecting matched subgroups before computing statistics.

software_tool.answer: ScanOMetrics; FreeSurfer; DL + DiReCT; PCN toolkit; BrainChart

response_variable.answer: Cortical GMV; mean and standard deviation of the CTh

predictor_effects.answer: Age is modeled as a fixed effect.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study accounts for nuisance variables such as age, sex, scanner, and scanning protocol.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: Covariates other than age (i.e. sex, scanner and scanning protocol) were accounted for by selecting matched subgroups before computing statistics.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The study uses a leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) to evaluate the normative dataset.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: The normative dataset was evaluated with a subject-wise leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) study, building normative polynomial models under exclusion of a specific HC (all sessions and repeated scans) and testing all scans of the excluded subject against that model, similar to what was described above for patients.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study does not use an independent dataset from the same domain for validation.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study does not use a dataset from a different domain for validation.

clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Regardless of the software used for extraction of the metrics, in patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD) anomaly detections were up to twenty-fold more frequent than in healthy controls (HC).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Cortical thickness (CTh) anomalies were mainly detected in regions that are known as predilection areas of cortical atrophy in AD. Atrophy patterns extend to larger regions when stratifying by clinical dementia rating (CDR) was clearly observable with both methods. DL + DiReCT provided CTh results more than 15 times faster than FreeSurfer.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The study did not investigate the heterogeneity/similarity of atrophy patterns across dementia subtypes.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The authors suggest that future work should combine residues from normative modeling with proportional hazard models for AD conversion, AD classifiers, or disease progression models to thoroughly investigate if improved diagnostic accuracy can be obtained at the subject level.
